claims.statement: The offline documentation review traverses all 13 required product guides and checks a curated set of significant sections for claim labels, scope limits and local evidence. Current workflow, verification-command and browser-fixture descriptions match their inspected source contracts rather than stale demo-only or unimplemented-aggregate statements.

The reviewed guides distinguish credential-free deterministic mocks and networked dependency acquisition from deferred credential-bearing provider work. They preserve the assumption register and explicit local self-approval, host trust, web outbound, retention, optional PostgreSQL and remote exactly-once limitations.

The dated AC-17 documentation review identifies the inspected product baseline, separates source review from product reruns, preserves historical results and their limitations, and explicitly leaves AC-15, AC-16 and final-source acceptance unverified. Command availability or successful documentation checks do not promote those targets to verified behavior.

Copied-root controls delete or misclassify significant claim distinctions, remove evidence and restore stale scopes; the bounded checker rejects them without executing examples or fetching external pages. A separate witness restores only corrected guides to main while retaining the new checker/tests and must fail for documentation content.

limitations: This acceptance requirement is a documentation-reading journey, not a browser, worker, provider or deployment journey. It changes no application, adapter, database, network enforcement, Docker settings or CI behavior.

Curated section contracts and negative controls catch specific omissions and regressions; they are not a semantic proof of arbitrary prose. Independent source review supplements the mechanical tests, and referenced historical behavior tests were not rerun by AC-17.
The inspection baseline is main after AC-14. The unmerged AC-15 checkpoint and separate diagnostics remain unchanged, and AC-15, AC-16 and final-source acceptance remain unverified.
All documentation checks are offline, read-only source consumers. This does not establish kernel-level network isolation for arbitrary test subprocesses or complete the four full AC-15 suites.

Real provider credentials and delivery, optional PostgreSQL runtime, physical retention maintenance, multi-user production identity and remote exactly-once effects are not qualified by documentation checks.
GitHub CI remains paused by user direction. No remote checks, publication or history rewrite are part of this requirement; historical verification dates, outcomes and limitations are preserved.
